subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Which subset of canonical readiness conditions, standard and operator profiles, plugin callbacks, activation identity, and release-conformance obligations should OpenClaw accept now?
rationale: The proposal and exact-head implementation evidence establish feasibility, but only maintainers can choose the permanent core API, failure policy, compatibility boundary, and release support promise.

options.title: Accept proven foundation
options.body: Approve canonical conditions, compatibility projections, and demonstrated initial profile and provider surfaces while deferring incomplete activation and release-gate obligations.

options.title: Accept complete roadmap
options.body: Approve all response, plugin, configuration, identity, and profile-support obligations as one long-term contract after full upgrade proof.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Keep hosting-readiness composition host- or plugin-owned rather than establishing this core support contract.

recommendation.title: Accept proven foundation
recommendation.body: Approve canonical conditions, compatibility projections, and demonstrated initial profile and provider surfaces while deferring incomplete activation and release-gate obligations.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the repository acceptance lifecycle and are the strongest history-backed routing candidate for advancing this draft through formal product direction.
